oneliner.t: Former NFL placekicker (14 seasons, 2001–2014, including the Arizona Cardinals 2010–2013) turned CBS analyst, from Gilbert. A first-time candidate, he launched in AZ-05 in April 2025, moved to AZ-01 in December 2025, and with Trump's endorsement won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary over state Rep. Joseph Chaplik. He faces Democrat Amish Shah and Libertarian Monica Alponte.

hometown.t: Tampa area, Florida (Jesuit High School, Tampa)

upbringing.t: Grew up in the Tampa area. His father, T.J. Feely, a former College of St. Thomas running back, owns the Feely Kicking School of Tampa, and his grandfather coached basketball and baseball at St. Thomas. At Tampa's Jesuit High School he set Hillsborough County kicking records, and at 16 he played on a national-champion youth soccer team. He kicked for Michigan from 1994 to 1998, including the 1997 national-title team. Undrafted in 1999, he played arena football before reaching the NFL with Atlanta in 2001. He and his wife, Rebecca, have four children and live in Gilbert.

education.deg: Attended; four-year football letterman (1994–1998). Degree not documented.

career.role: NFL placekicker: Falcons 2001–04, Giants 2005–06, Dolphins 2007, Jets 2008–09, Cardinals 2010–13, Bears 2014
College football analyst (CBS Sports Network), then NFL color commentator/sideline reporter on CBS from 2017; about $220K CBS income in 2024
Investor: stakes in Gevity Health, Klein Tools and Kumanu; four rental homes

platform.t: Described himself in April 2025 as a fiscal conservative, a social conservative and 'pro-business.'
Wants tighter regulation of college NIL (name, image and likeness) deals.
Runs as a close Trump ally: Trump endorsed him in the primary, and he was the only Arizona candidate to speak at the September 2026 RNC convention, where he praised Trump.
Says he will not run 'based on slandering people' or attack opponents' personal lives.

promises.t: Keep boys out of girls' sports.
Economic growth and middle-class tax cuts.

record.t: No public office appears in his record. His career was in pro football and broadcasting.

claims.claim: Says both Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson asked him to run in the 1st District.
claims.short: Trump, Johnson asked him to switch

record.t: Cronkite News reports he switched at Trump's request, to clear AZ-05 for Mark Lamb, with an endorsement offered. At the Dec 19, 2025 switch, KTAR noted Trump had endorsed Gina Swoboda in CD1, and Feely's own statement cited consulting 'Republican leadership' without naming Trump or Johnson. Johnson's role is not independently documented.

claims.claim: Called Shah one of the 'Democrat socialists like Bernie Sanders' and accused him of backing a socialized health system.

record.t: Shah does not call himself a democratic socialist. KJZZ reports he has never said he supports socialized (government-run) health care; he backs universal access to affordable care.

claims.claim: Said Democrats like Sanders and Shah have articulated visions to 'abolish prisons, abolish borders, abolish the U.S. Senate.'

record.t: As applied to Shah, no record of him supporting any of the three was found. His documented platform includes securing the U.S.–Mexico border.

claims.claim: Branded primary rival Joseph Chaplik 'No Show Joe' (his campaign also bought noshowjoechaplik.com).

said.where: campaign nickname and website, per Cronkite News

record.t: Chaplik sent a cease-and-desist letter alleging libel about his voting record. His legislative attendance was not checked.

entries.t: Launched a run for AZ-05 to succeed Andy Biggs.
Switched to AZ-01 on Dec 19, 2025, saying 'no one player is more important than the well-being of the team.'

corp.t: Non-party committees (PACs) gave $323,329.55 in 2025–26, 20% of his contributions; the FEC summary does not split business from ideological PACs. Named sports-industry donors include NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell ($7,000) and the Cardinals-owning Bidwill family ($17,000 combined), with Robert Kraft, Charles Barkley and Jim Nantz also giving (amounts not stated). Whether one industry reaches 10% of itemized money was not computed.

money2.note: Bidwill family (Michael, Nicole and Tim) gave $17,000 combined. Kraft, Barkley, Nantz and Arthur Blank also gave; amounts were not stated (Fox News, Jul 2026).

note.t: Per Sportico: 2024 income $453K–$1.52M, including about $220K from CBS and $35K from radio ads for Yrefy, a private student-loan company. Holdings include Palantir stock ($500K–$1M), seven-figure stakes in Gevity Health and Klein Tools, a $500K–$1M stake in Kumanu (digital mental health), NFL pension and annuity ($1M–$5M each), a Gilbert home and four rental homes (two in Arizona, two in Michigan).

Cronkite News says he has lived in the 5th District for 12 years (Gilbert); he is running in the neighboring 1st. Arizona has no requirement that U.S. House candidates live in the district. He played for the Cardinals 2010–2013.

research_notes: az-races.json records his primary result as 49.8% to Chaplik's 35.7%; that page was not reopened here. When he switched districts (Dec 2025) Trump had endorsed Gina Swoboda in CD1; Trump later endorsed Feely. A Fox News article in the sample misstates the per-election contribution limit, so only its named-donor facts were used. 314 Action Fund's ad says he backed Trump's tariffs and praised the Iran war; those are opponent characterizations not verified here. AP: he and Shah overlapped with the Jets in 2008–09, when Shah was a sideline airway physician.
